method_note: All claim texts come from the consolidated Regulation (EU) No 432/2012 (20.08.2025) in English and Italian, cross-checked against the EU Register data feed (register_claim_en and register_matches_regulation). Composition values come from CREA (alimentinutrizione.it, pages fetched 2026-11-06), ANSES CIQUAL 2020 (Zenodo copy of the official English table; ciqual.anses.fr returned HTTP 503) and USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy (April 2018 CSV). Values reported as traces or below a quantification limit are stored as 0 and listed in value_flags. null means not reported.

claims.claim_en: DHA contributes to maintenance of normal brain function
claims.claim_it: Il DHA contribuisce al mantenimento della normale funzione cerebrale
claims.conditions_en: At least 40 mg DHA per 100 g and per 100 kcal; consumer told the effect needs 250 mg DHA per day.
claims.conditions_en_full: The claim may be used only for food which contains at least 40 mg of DHA per 100 g and per 100 kcal. In order to bear the claim information shall be given to the consumer that the beneficial effect is obtained with a daily intake of 250 mg of DHA.

thresholds.nrv_note: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex XIII Part A point 1 (consolidated 01.04.2025). Folate NRV is listed there as "Folic acid (microgram) 200".
thresholds.source_of_rule: SOURCE OF [VITAMIN/MINERAL] (Reg. (EC) 1924/2006 Annex): the product contains at least a significant amount as defined in the Annex to Directive 90/496/EEC; that Directive was repealed by Reg. (EU) 1169/2011 (Art. 53: references are read as references to 1169/2011). Annex XIII Part A point 2: as a rule 15% of the NRV supplied by 100 g or 100 ml for products other than beverages, 7.5% of the NRV per 100 ml for beverages, or 15% of the NRV per portion if the package contains only a single portion. HIGH [VITAMIN/MINERAL] = at least twice the source value.
thresholds.protein_rule: SOURCE OF PROTEIN: at least 12% of the energy value of the food is provided by protein. HIGH PROTEIN: at least 20%. (Reg. (EC) 1924/2006 Annex.) Energy computed with Reg. (EU) 1169/2011 Annex XIV factors: protein 4 kcal/g, carbohydrate 4, fat 9, fibre 2, polyols 2.4, alcohol 7, organic acid 3, salatrims 6, erythritol 0.
thresholds.fibre_rule: SOURCE OF FIBRE: at least 3 g fibre per 100 g or at least 1.5 g fibre per 100 kcal. HIGH FIBRE: at least 6 g per 100 g or at least 3 g per 100 kcal. (Reg. (EC) 1924/2006 Annex.)
thresholds.omega3_rule: SOURCE OF OMEGA-3 FATTY ACIDS: at least 0.3 g alpha-linolenic acid per 100 g and per 100 kcal, or at least 40 mg of the sum of eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid per 100 g and per 100 kcal. HIGH OMEGA-3: 0.6 g ALA or 80 mg EPA+DHA, per 100 g and per 100 kcal. (Reg. (EC) 1924/2006 Annex, as amended by Reg. (EU) No 116/2010.)

other_rules.low_sodium: LOW SODIUM/SALT: no more than 0.12 g sodium (or equivalent salt) per 100 g or 100 ml; VERY LOW: no more than 0.04 g; SODIUM-FREE: no more than 0.005 g.
other_rules.high_unsaturated_fat: HIGH UNSATURATED FAT: at least 70% of the fatty acids present derive from unsaturated fat, under the condition that unsaturated fat provides more than 20% of energy of the product.
other_rules.naturally_prefix: Where a food naturally meets the conditions for a nutrition claim, the term "naturally/natural" may be used as a prefix to the claim (Reg. (EC) 1924/2006 Annex, introductory text).

rules_it.fibre: FONTE DI FIBRE: L'indicazione che un alimento è fonte di fibre e ogni altra indicazione che può avere lo stesso significato per il consumatore sono consentite solo se il prodotto contiene almeno 3 g di fibre per 100 g o almeno 1,5 g di fibre per 100 kcal.
rules_it.protein: FONTE DI PROTEINE: L'indicazione che un alimento è fonte di proteine e ogni altra indicazione che può avere lo stesso significato per il consumatore sono consentite solo se almeno il 12 % del valore energetico dell'alimento è apportato da proteine.
rules_it.omega3: FONTE DI ACIDI GRASSI OMEGA-3: L'indicazione che un alimento è fonte di acidi grassi omega-3 e ogni altra indicazione che può avere lo stesso significato per il consumatore sono consentite solo se il prodotto contiene almeno 0,3 g di acido alfa-linolenico per 100 g e per 100 kcal oppure almeno 40 mg della somma di acido eicosapentanoico e acido docosaesaenoico per 100 g e per 100 kcal.

open_questions: System enum gaps: no value fits vision (DHA), thyroid (iodine, selenium), tiredness and fatigue (vitamin C, iron, folate, B12, magnesium, B6) or cell protection from oxidative stress (vitamin E). Used closest enum value plus system_alt (eyes, thyroid, energy_fatigue, cells_whole_body). Suggest adding "eyes", "thyroid" and "energy" to the enum.

No authorised claim in this set links any food or nutrient to the kidneys, liver, joints or skin. The app must not imply kidney benefits; the only kidney-adjacent item is sodium reduction for blood pressure (system_alt kidneys).

Lupus nephritis safety: potassium and protein claims are positive messages in EU law, but with kidney involvement potassium (and phosphorus) may need restriction. Ask the nephrologist and nutritionist before showing "source of potassium" as a benefit; consider hiding the potassium claims or showing them neutrally.

Celiac disease: oats (fiocchi di avena, pasta di avena) are acceptable only if labelled gluten-free; buckwheat, millet, sorghum, quinoa and rice products need gluten-free labelling to exclude cross-contamination. Not a nutrition-claim issue but affects which products the app should name.

Beta-glucan, olive oil polyphenols (hydroxytyrosol) and cocoa flavanols are not reported by CREA, CIQUAL 2020 or USDA SR Legacy, so these claims cannot be linked from composition data. Need product labels or producer analyses.
Walnut (30 g/day), prune (100 g/day) and kiwi (200 g/day) claims require the daily amount; the app must check the plan portions before showing them.

Several plan foods have no exact database entry and use proxies: buckwheat flakes, puffed brown rice, puffed quinoa, buckwheat cakes, buckwheat pasta, brown rice pasta, oat pasta. Product labels would be better than proxies for these.

Light/brand dairy (ricotta light, mozzarella light, philadelphia light, fiocchi di latte) use USDA generic products because CREA and CIQUAL lack them or report macros only; Italian products may differ (often lower fat). Labels recommended.

Primary database rule used: CREA when the CREA entry is the same food and state and reports energy, macronutrients, fibre and at least 4 of calcium, iron, magnesium, potassium, sodium; otherwise CIQUAL 2020; otherwise USDA SR Legacy. Missing nutrients are filled from the same food in CIQUAL, then USDA, and every filled value is listed in nutrient_sources. CREA reports fatty acids only as % of total fatty acids, so EPA, DHA and ALA always come from CIQUAL or USDA. Is this mixed approach acceptable, or should one database be used per food even if it leaves gaps?

Energy: CREA uses its own (Southgate) energy and expresses available carbohydrate as monosaccharide equivalents; CIQUAL gives energy per Reg. (EU) 1169/2011; USDA uses Atwater factors. The protein rule uses each primary database energy value; the protein check is marked borderline when the result is between 9.6% and 15%.
Sodium is reported per 100 g; canned and brined foods (olives, tuna, smoked salmon, ham, canned chickpeas) vary by brand and rinsing.

source_of is the strict computation required by the brief. source_of_recommended removes borderline results, cross-database disagreements, known database artefacts and soil-dependent selenium/iodine in plant foods. Recommend the app shows only source_of_recommended.

Zinc, selenium, iodine, vitamin E and vitamin B6 were not in the requested composition list but have claims in Task A, so they were added in per100g_extra (mostly from CIQUAL). Treat them as secondary.
